title: Viscohypoplastic bentonite (VIBE, Mašín2026)
summary: VIBE combines swelling within clay aggregates, deformation between aggregates and elapsed time to describe the coupled stress and water-retention response of bentonite.
introduction: The model treats the fine pores within clay aggregates and the larger pores between aggregates separately. Swelling of the fine structure can compress the larger pores even when the specimen volume is fixed. Temperature and suction influence both structures, while a viscous stress contribution allows relaxation during a hold.

behaviours.title: Stress relaxation during a hold
behaviours.explanation: With viscosity enabled, stress can change while total strain, suction and temperature are held fixed. The temperature coefficient controls how this time effect grows as the specimen heats.

behaviours.title: Wetting and drying follow different branches
behaviours.explanation: The hydraulic memory records whether the material follows a main wetting branch, a main drying branch or an intermediate scanning path. The water stored in the fine and larger pores combines into the total saturation.

behaviours.title: Internal swelling differs from external loading
behaviours.explanation: The model reduces irreversible deformation caused internally by swelling and shrinking of aggregates, while preserving a nonlinear response to an externally imposed load.

parameterNote: The source parameter set describes BCV bentonite. Pressures use pascals, temperature uses kelvins and loading rate uses inverse seconds. Compression and unloading slopes refer to logarithmic pressure and void-ratio relations. Reference pressure and the listed hidden constants are part of the formulation; changing the reference pressure without changing the intercept changes the material.
preparation: Supply initial net stress, void ratio, hydraulic branch, suction and absolute temperature. Void ratio can be calculated from solid density divided by dry density minus one. A branch value of zero represents powder-compacted material on the wetting branch; one represents the drying branch. Microvoid ratio, macrovoid ratio and both saturations are calculated from that current context. A software starting example does not reproduce the specimen preparation history.
scope: This profile describes the published explicit Appendix A formulation of Mašín2026. The intended implementation uses physical time, prescribed thermal and hydraulic histories, and net stress: total stress with the pore-air contribution removed. Availability of an interactive laboratory is determined by the installed model route.
limits: The first proposed executable domain has strictly positive suction and compressive effective pressures. A saturated start is excluded because the published hydraulic-memory equation has an unresolved zero-suction boundary. The proposed host uses a fixed frame and small strains; it supplies no finite-rotation update or field solution for heat transfer and water flow. Very long time predictions extrapolate beyond the duration of the cited experiments.
equationIntro: The explicit formulation evolves net stress and two internal memories; other pore-structure quantities are calculated from the current state.

equations.label: Global void ratio
equations.equation: e_dot=(1+e) tr(strain_rate), in the source compression-negative convention.

equationNote: The selected explicit Appendix A law contains separate absolute hydraulic and thermal contributions. The paper body also presents a combined absolute-value form; these differ for opposing simultaneous contributions and are not claimed equivalent. Tensor-rank omissions in the Appendix are resolved by its body derivation.
